identity.name: Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic
native_names: საქართველოს საბჭოთა სოციალისტური რესპუბლიკა (Sakartvelos Sabch'ota Sotsialist'uri Respublik'a)

land.text: Cliopatria's Georgia of 1920-1921, the Democratic Republic of Georgia

predecessors.note: The Red Army entered Tbilisi on 25 February 1921 and the Democratic Republic's government went into exile in March 1921.

successors.note: Renamed the Republic of Georgia on 14 November 1990; independence declared 9 April 1991, recognised 26 December 1991.

capitals.name: Tbilisi
capitals.note: Infobox: Tbilisi. It was also the seat of the Transcaucasian SFSR, 1922-1936.

correction.text: Georgia within Natural Earth borders, including Abkhazia, South Ossetia and Adjara

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 69,042 km2 (the Natural Earth country, which includes Abkhazia and South Ossetia; the page gives no area): Soviet Georgia in the borders it kept from the Treaty of Kars (13 October 1921) to 1991. Cliopatria's Georgia of 1920-1921 is 72,683 km2, about 3,600 km2 larger, and holds nothing for 1922-1991 (the land lies inside its Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes). The republic ceded the Artvin Okrug to Turkey and kept Adjara, which was an Adjar ASSR from 16 July 1921. During 1922-1936 the land is drawn as the Transcaucasian federation (ledger). [Reviewer eu-17-x: this keyframe now ends in 1921; from 12 March 1922 to 5 December 1936 the land is the Transcaucasian SFSR's (ledger loss and gain, and that dossier's keyframe); the same shape resumes in the 1937 keyframe.]

region.text: Tbilisi and its district at the fall of the capital

ledger.note: 1921, 25 February: "On 25 February, after a one-week offence by the Red Army, Tbilisi fell to the Bolsheviks" and the Revolutionary Committee "declared the Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic on 25 February 1921".

region.text: Georgia within Natural Earth borders, including Abkhazia, South Ossetia and Adjara

ledger.note: 1921, March: the rest of Georgia passes to the Soviet side as the invasion (12 February to 17 March 1921) ends; "In March 1921 the government of the Georgian Democratic Republic was forced into exile" and Batumi is surrendered to the Revkom. The pages give no dated list of districts.

region.text: the Artvin Okrug, the southern half of the former Batum oblast, approximated by Turkey's Artvin Province

ledger.note: Page silent on whether the Georgian SSR held or administered the Artvin Okrug before the Treaty of Kars; it is drawn from the invasion's end (March 1921) because the page says the republic was "forced to cede the Georgian-dominated Artvin Okrug to Turkey".

region.text: the Artvin Okrug, the southern half of the former Batum oblast, approximated by Turkey's Artvin Province

ledger.note: 1921, 13 October: the Treaty of Kars: the southern half of the former Batum oblast, "largely the Artvin okrug", "would be annexed to Turkey"; "The Georgian SSR was forced to cede the Georgian-dominated Artvin Okrug to Turkey in exchange for keeping Adjara." Turkey received free transit through Batumi; the northern half stays in Georgia.

ledger.note: 1922, 12 March: "From March 12, 1922, to December 5, 1936, it was part of the Transcaucasian SFSR together with the Armenian SSR and the Azerbaijan SSR." The land is drawn as the federation.

ledger.note: 1936, 5 December: "In 1936, the TSFSR was dissolved and Georgia became the Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic" (infobox: TSFSR dissolved 5 December 1936; "1936-1990: Union republic of the Soviet Union").

1990, 14 November: "Renamed to Republic of Georgia: 14 November 1990" (sovereignty declared 9 March 1990; "On November 14 a transitional period was declared until the restoration of Georgia's independence").

wars.name: Red Army invasion of Georgia

zones.text: Georgia within Natural Earth borders, including Abkhazia, South Ossetia and Adjara

wars.outcome: The invasion ran from 12 February to 17 March 1921; the Red Army entered Tbilisi on 25 February; the Georgian government went into exile; the Treaty of Kars (13 October 1921) "contained the provisions agreed upon in March".
wars.note: Whether Turkish troops held Batumi, Artvin or Ardahan in March 1921 is not on the pages opened.

certainty.note: The Batum oblast changed hands between February and October 1921; the page gives no district-level dates.
Treaty of Kars border with Turkey; the Abkhazia and South Ossetia lines are the republic's internal boundaries, not on the pages opened.

sources.title: Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: 25 February 1921 fall of Tbilisi; TSFSR 12 March 1922 to 5 December 1936; Kars cession of the Artvin Okrug; sovereignty 9 March 1990; renamed 14 November 1990; independence 9 April 1991; capital Tbilisi; no area.

sources.title: Soviet invasion of Georgia
sources.note: 12 February to 17 March 1921; Tbilisi entered 25 February; Batumi surrendered; Georgian SSR declared 25 February 1921; Kars signed 13 October 1921.

sources.title: Treaty of Kars
sources.note: 13 October 1921: Kars oblast, Surmalu uezd and the southern Batum oblast (Artvin) to Turkey; the northern half (Batum okrug) to Soviet Georgia as the Adjar ASSR; Nakhchivan under Azerbaijan; no areas.

sources.title: Transcaucasian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic
sources.note: Adjar ASSR 16 July 1921; Abkhazia treaty republic 16 December 1921, ASSR 19 February 1931; TSFSR 1922-1936.

notes: No Cliopatria row after 1921: Cliopatria's Georgia (shapes 1918, 1919, 1920-1921) is the Democratic Republic and the 1992 shape is the modern state; the Soviet years lie inside Union of Soviet Socialist Republics shapes (1922-1991) and Republics of the Soviet Union (1920-1921). The republic is an internal unit of the Soviet Union. Model: 1922-1936 the land is lent to the Transcaucasian federation (ledger loss and gain; the TSFSR dossier mirrors it). The Artvin Okrug is a reading: the pages say it was ceded but give no date of Georgian administration, so the gain is confidence 1. The Treaty of Kars page does not name Georgia as a ceding party; the Georgian SSR page does. Abkhazia (SSR Abkhazia in a treaty union with Georgia from 16 December 1921, an ASSR from 19 February 1931), the Adjar ASSR (16 July 1921) and the South Ossetian AO (1922, not dated by any page opened) are inside the drawn land. Counterparts: georgia exists (Cliopatria); ottoman-empire is used for the Grand National Assembly government that signed Kars, as Cliopatria's Republic of Turkey begins in 1924.
